judgments.reasoning_cat1: The elective part ('Change to paid-up insurance for $____') is blank, and the parenthetical that '{Any additional benefit provision attached to this policy] shall terminate according to its terms unless otherwise provided' leaves both which provisions terminate and what counts as 'otherwise provided' unfixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the separate cancellation of Supplementary Agreements (c015) and with c020's release of the insurer from claims under any cancelled part, so automatic termination of riders here could collide with c019's rule that benefits cannot change without the owner's written agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the standard tax notice that the payee remains liable for tax and may face estimated-tax penalties, but as reproduced it is a spliced fragment interleaved with the paid-up insurance and rating clauses, so the sentence as written does not read coherently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits with the withholding instructions and elections (c010, c014, c016, c017) and creates no contradiction with any operative policy-change term; the splicing is a column artifact rather than a drafting conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The election to 'remove or reduce rating' with future monthly insurance costs 'charged based on the reduced or removed rating' is a clear cost rule, though it fixes no effective date and 'rating' is undefined on the form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with c019, a rating change is a change in 'risk class' that requires the owner's written agreement, and with the Home Office Endorsement block that permits corrections; those provisions are broadly compatible with this election.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line election that the owner does not want Federal income tax withheld from the distribution — definite, self-contained, and doing exactly what it says.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by c017's rule that a missing Social Security number produces 20% withholding regardless, which is the only place in the instrument that cuts against the election.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Cancel the following Supplementary Agreement(s) from the policy' followed by a blank list; 'Supplementary Agreement' is not defined on the form and the list is empty, so the reach of the cancellation is not settled by the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with c011's parenthetical that additional benefit provisions terminate according to their terms and with c020's release of liability for any cancelled part, so the two cancellation routes must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The affirmative withholding election is a single definite sentence electing to have Federal income tax withheld from the distribution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mirror of c014 and is governed by the same instruction (c010) and default rule (c017); no other provision pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence conditions a flat 20% withholding on the owner's Social Security number not being completed, and as written it is grammatically broken ('you be subject to a 20% withholding') and switches between the owner and 'you', leaving it unclear whose number and whose distribution is meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly qualifies, and on its face overrides, the box A election not to have any Federal income tax withheld (c014) and the instruction in c010, which is the closest thing on this form to a conflicting pair.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A representation that no bankruptcy proceedings, attachment, tax or other lien claim is 'pending against me' — the list of specifics followed by 'other lien claim' invites an ejusdem generis argument, and 'pending' is undefined as to threatened or unfiled claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the assignment questions (c003, c005) and the assignee-consent block, all of which concern competing interests in the policy, but nothing in the instrument contradicts the representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause both deems acceptance of the policy or policy change to ratify any correction or change the Home Office noted under 'Home Office Endorsement' and then carves out that there can be no change in amount, age at issue, risk class, plan or benefits without the owner's written agreement, so the ratification and the carve-out define each other and the residue of what may be corrected is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears directly on the actual endorsement executed on this form ('ENDORSE BY ATTACHMENT effective December 4/1995') and on the amount, rating and benefit changes elected at c006, c013 and c015, and whether acceptance ratified those is exactly the sort of whole-instrument question this form raises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If any part of the policy is cancelled by a change, Ohio National will be released from any claims or liability under such part' turns on the undefined boundary of 'any part' and 'cancelled by a change', and the follow-on that 'premium adjustments will then be made' states no measure or direction of adjustment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with c019's bar on changes in amount or benefits absent written agreement, with the paid-up election's termination parenthetical (c011) and with the cancellation of supplementary agreements (c015); a release triggered automatically by 'a change' sits awkwardly against c019's consent requirement.
